useCase.name: Put a vacancy on the school website so candidates can apply, and take it down when it closes

intent.name: website.posting.publish
intent.summary: Put a vacancy on the careers page so candidates can find it and apply. The screen calls this listing a vacancy.
routesHere: list the senior physics teacher post on the website

routesHere.text: physics teacher ki vacancy website pe laga do
routesHere.gloss: put the physics teacher vacancy on the website

routesHere.text: naye post ka ishtihaar site pe daal dein
routesHere.gloss: please put the advertisement for the new post on the site

routesHere.text: careers page pe ye jagah live kar dein
routesHere.gloss: make this post live on the careers page

request.text: mujhe is post ke liye apply karna hai
request.gloss: I want to apply for this post

routesElsewhere.goesTo: No intent. The careers page on the public website only.
routesElsewhere.note: A candidate applies through the form on the site, with no login and no session to plan against. The application is recorded against the vacancy in recruitment, and nothing about it is held here (BR-4, AC-4).

request.text: is post ke liye shortlist kar dein
request.gloss: shortlist for this post

routesElsewhere.note: Shortlisting, interviews and the appointment decision are recruitment. This use case controls only the posting on the site (BR-7, AC-11).

request.text: posting mein requirements badal do
request.gloss: change the requirements on the posting

routesElsewhere.note: There is no such field on the posting. The role, requirements and closing date are carried from the vacancy rather than retyped, because a posting that says something different from the vacancy is a posting the school cannot stand behind (BR-3, E4, AC-3).

request.text: pehle vacancy bana do phir laga do
request.gloss: create the vacancy first and then list it

routesElsewhere.note: Two acts in two modules. The vacancy carries the role, the requirements, the closing date and the salary budget; the posting carries the vacancy to the public (BR-2).

request.text: tankhwah bhi likh dein posting mein
request.gloss: put the salary in the posting as well

routesElsewhere.note: The posting does not show the salary range. Whether it should is an open question this use case raises and does not answer, and the salary budget is subject to the visibility rule in HR (OQ-4).

routesElsewhere.request: write a news item saying we are hiring
routesElsewhere.note: A news item is written wording. A posting is a vacancy carried whole, and the two are different acts.

steps.note: One step, and it takes the vacancy rather than any wording: the role, requirements and closing date are carried from it (BR-3, AC-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where the website cannot be reached nothing is listed and it is reported, rather than the posting appearing to have gone up (BR-10, E5, AC-10).
plan.atomicity: One write and one outbound call, together: the posting on the careers page and the row recording who listed it and when. Nothing about the vacancy itself changes — this is the vacancy made public, not a copy of it.

operations.name: website.posting.publish
operations.idempotencyKey: vacancy_id, since a vacancy is advertised once at a time and a repeat must not put two copies of the same post on the careers page
operations.purpose: List an open vacancy on the school's careers page.

parameters.name: vacancy_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open vacancy matches. The vacancy is created in recruitment before it can be listed on the website (E2, AC-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the open vacancies that match with their department and closing date.

parameters.notes: The vacancy, named the way the school names the post. It is a vacancy created in recruitment — there is no route that lists a post the school has not opened (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What is now on the careers page, and what it carries.

fields.name: posting_id
fields.description: The posting.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Carried from the vacancy, not typed (BR-3).

fields.name: requirements
fields.description: Carried from the vacancy (BR-3).

fields.name: closing_date
fields.description: Carried from the vacancy. The posting comes down after it (BR-5).

fields.name: listed_by
fields.description: Who listed it (BR-6).

fields.name: listed_on
fields.description: When.

fields.name: public_url
fields.description: The careers page address, read and applied to with no login.

fields.name: applications_go_to
fields.description: Recruitment, against this vacancy. Nothing about an application is held here (BR-4, AC-4).

errors.meaning: No vacancy exists for the post.
errors.note: There is no route that lists a post the school has not opened. The vacancy is created in recruitment first (BR-2, AC-1).

errors.meaning: The vacancy's closing date has already passed.
errors.note: A posting past its closing date collects applications the school will not answer (BR-5).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: The posting is not on the site.
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to have gone up (BR-10, AC-10). The integration retries three times first.

planningRules.rule: Never type the role, the requirements or the closing date. They are carried from the vacancy, and a posting that says something different from the vacancy is a posting the school cannot stand behind (BR-3, E4, AC-2).

Never list a post with no vacancy behind it. The vacancy is created in recruitment first — that is where the role, the requirements, the closing date and the salary budget are decided (BR-2, E2, AC-1).
Say where applications go. They are recorded against the vacancy in recruitment, not here, and a school that expects them on the website screen watches the wrong list (BR-4, AC-4).
Say when the posting comes down. It goes after the closing date without anybody acting, and earlier where the vacancy is filled or withdrawn (BR-5, BR-11).
Never offer to show the salary. The posting does not carry it, and whether it should is unanswered — the salary budget is subject to a visibility rule in HR (OQ-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: The posting comes off the careers page with a reason recorded (BR-5, BR-6). Applications already made are unaffected — an application received is an application that must still be answered (BR-8, AC-8) — and the posting stays on the record, because a candidate may ask afterwards what the post said (BR-9).

request.text: physics teacher ki vacancy website pe laga do
request.gloss: put the physics teacher vacancy on the website

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin holding the website permission, Johar Town branch, with the vacancy open in recruitment.

steps.note: The wording comes from the vacancy, untouched (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report what went up — the role, the requirements and the closing date as the vacancy holds them — and that it comes down after that date on its own. Add that applications arrive in recruitment against this vacancy, not on the website screen, and that the posting carries no salary.

request.text: hamein ek aur maths teacher chahiye, site pe laga dein
request.gloss: we need another maths teacher, put it on the site

resolvedPlans.context: Staff member holding the permission, with no vacancy created.

steps.note: Refused at resolution. There is no route that lists a post the school has not opened (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is listed. Say that the vacancy is created in recruitment first — that is where the role, the requirements, the closing date and the salary budget are set, and the posting carries them rather than inventing them. Listing follows once it exists.

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, with the vacancy's closing date three days past.

steps.note: Refused. The closing date has passed (PR-4 explains when a posting comes down).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the vacancy closed and that listing it would collect applications the school will not answer. If the post is still open, the closing date is extended on the vacancy in recruitment — not on the posting, which carries whatever the vacancy says.

intent.name: website.posting.remove
intent.summary: Take a posting off the careers page, with the reason recorded. A filled vacancy left up collects applications the school cannot answer.
routesHere: take the physics teacher post off the site, we have appointed somebody

routesHere.text: physics teacher wali posting hata do, banda rakh liya hai
routesHere.gloss: take the physics teacher posting down, we have taken somebody on

routesHere.text: ye jagah ab nahi chahiye, site se utaar dein
routesHere.gloss: we no longer need this post, please take it off the site
take the posting off the site

request.text: vacancy hi band kar do
request.gloss: close the vacancy itself

routesElsewhere.note: Closing the vacancy in recruitment takes the posting down with it — a vacancy closed and a posting still up must not disagree (BR-11, A1). Removing the posting alone leaves the vacancy open.

request.text: jo applications aa chuki hain wo bhi cancel kar dein
request.gloss: cancel the applications that have already come in too

routesElsewhere.note: An application already made is unaffected by the posting coming down. An application received is an application that must still be answered (BR-8, AC-8).

routesElsewhere.request: delete the posting so nobody can see what it said
routesElsewhere.note: A posting is removed, never deleted, and the record of what was advertised stays. A candidate may ask afterwards what the post said (BR-9, E7, AC-9).

request.text: closing date par khud hat jaye
request.gloss: let it come off on the closing date by itself

routesElsewhere.note: The posting is removed after the closing date without anybody acting (BR-5). This capability is for taking it down earlier.

steps.note: One step. The posting leaves the careers page with the reason recorded (BR-5, BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A removal with no reason is refused (E6), and where the website cannot be reached the posting is still on the site and nothing is recorded as removed (BR-10, E5).
plan.atomicity: One write and one outbound call, together: the posting off the careers page and the row in its history. Every application already made is untouched (BR-8), including one submitted as the posting came down (A5).

operations.name: website.posting.remove
operations.idempotencyKey: posting_id, since a posting leaves the site once and a repeat is the retry of a removal that did not reach the site
operations.purpose: Take a posting off the careers page with the reason recorded.

parameters.name: posting_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No listed posting matches that description.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the postings currently on the site with their closing dates.

parameters.notes: The posting on the site, named by its role.

parameters.name: removal_reason
parameters.type: enum: Vacancy filled|Vacancy withdrawn|Taken down by hand
parameters.notes: Why the posting came down (BR-5, E6). Closing date passed is the fourth value the field holds and it belongs to the removal the System makes when the date passes — a person taking a posting down says which of the other three it was.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What came off and what survives it.

fields.name: posting_id
fields.description: The posting.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Removed. Off the site and on the record (BR-9).

fields.name: removed_by
fields.description: Who removed it (BR-6).

fields.name: removal_reason
fields.description: Why.

fields.name: days_listed
fields.description: How long it stood on the careers page.

fields.name: applications_while_up
fields.description: How many it attracted. They are recorded in recruitment, are unaffected by this, and still have to be answered (BR-4, BR-8, AC-8).

fields.name: vacancy_still_open
fields.description: Whether the vacancy behind it is still open in recruitment. Removing the posting does not close the vacancy — only the advertisement comes down.

errors.meaning: No reason was given for removing the posting.
errors.notWritten: The posting stays on the site.

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
errors.notWritten: The posting stays on the site.

errors.meaning: The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: The posting is still on the site and nothing is recorded as removed.
errors.note: Reported rather than the posting appearing to have changed (BR-10, AC-10).

planningRules.rule: Never give Closing date passed as the reason for a removal a person asked for. That value belongs to the removal the System makes when the date arrives, and using it here records the date as having done what a person decided (BR-5, BR-6).

Say that removing the posting does not close the vacancy. The advertisement comes down; the vacancy stays open in recruitment, and a school that thinks the post is closed stops shortlisting for one that is not (BR-11).
Say that applications already received are unaffected. An application received is an application that must still be answered, and taking the advert down does not answer any of them (BR-8, AC-8).
Never offer deletion. A posting is removed and the record of what was advertised stays, because a candidate may ask afterwards what the post said (BR-9, E7, AC-9).
Report an unreachable website as still listed. A filled post that the school believes is off the site goes on collecting applications nobody is reading (BR-10, E5, AC-10).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A vacancy that reopens is listed again, and the earlier posting and its removal stay on the record (A4, BR-9). Nothing about the applications already received changes either way (BR-8).

request.text: physics teacher wali posting hata do, banda rakh liya hai
request.gloss: take the physics teacher posting down, we have taken somebody on

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin holding the website permission, Johar Town branch, posting up for 21 days with 23 applications.

steps.note: The reason is one of the three a person can give, taken from what they said (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that it is off the careers page and that the 23 applications stay in recruitment and still have to be answered — including the ones nobody shortlisted. Add that the vacancy itself is still open in recruitment unless somebody closes it there; only the advert came down.

request.text: posting hata do
request.gloss: take the posting down

resolvedPlans.context: Staff member holding the permission, one posting listed.

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The reason is required (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing comes down. Ask which it is — the post was filled, the post was withdrawn, or it is being taken down by hand for another reason. The closing date having passed is not one of the answers: the System does that removal itself.

operations.name: website.postings.read
operations.purpose: List job postings with their state, closing dates and application counts.

parameters.name: on_the_site
parameters.notes: Whether to answer about postings currently listed, or to reach back to removed ones as well.

parameters.name: closing_within_days
parameters.notes: Where the question is about what is closing soon.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What is advertised and what it has produced.

fields.name: postings
fields.description: Role, department, closing date, whether it is on the site, who listed it, when, and how many applications it has attracted.

fields.name: listed
fields.description: How many are on the careers page now.

fields.name: closing_soon
fields.description: Postings whose closing date is near, with the applications each has so far.

fields.name: no_applications
fields.description: Postings that have attracted none. A post advertised for three weeks with nothing against it is usually a post nobody can find or nobody can meet.

fields.name: vacancies_open_not_listed
fields.description: Vacancies open in recruitment with no posting on the site — the post the school is waiting to fill and has not advertised (BR-2, OQ-1).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the job postings screen.

planningRules.rule: Give applications against days listed. Two applications on a post advertised yesterday and two on one advertised a month ago are different facts, and a bare count reads as the first (BR-4).

Name the open vacancies with no posting. Listing is by hand as modelled and nothing prompts it, so a vacancy the school is waiting to fill can sit unadvertised without anybody noticing — recruitment cannot receive an application until the vacancy is on the site (BR-2, OQ-1).
Say that applications are counted here and held in recruitment. Nothing about an applicant is on this screen, and a school reading this list is not reading its candidates (BR-4, AC-4).
Never report a salary range from the vacancy. The posting does not carry it and the budget is subject to a visibility rule in HR (OQ-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kaunsi vacancies abhi site pe hain aur kitni applications aayi hain?
request.gloss: which vacancies are on the site now and how many applications have come in?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each posting with its closing date and its applications against the days it has been up. Add two things nobody asked for: the postings with no applications at all, and any vacancy open in recruitment that was never listed — nothing prompts the listing, so a post the school is waiting to fill can sit unadvertised.

Give the postings closing within the week with the applications each has. Say that they come off the site after the closing date on their own — and that a post closing with two applications is a decision to make before the date, not after, because relisting starts the advertisement again from nothing.

routesElsewhere.note: How many applied in a listing is here. Who they were, and what became of each, is recorded against the vacancy in recruitment (BR-4, AC-4).

routesElsewhere.note: A vacancy that reopens is listed again, and the earlier posting and its removal stay on the record (A4).

steps.note: One read of an append-only record — one row per listing and one per removal, with the reason (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where the question names a post nobody matches, ask rather than answering about a different one.
plan.atomicity: A read. The record is append only: a listing or a removal adds a row and never rewrites one (BR-6, BR-9).

operations.name: website.posting.history.read
operations.purpose: Return the listing and removal history of postings, with what each listing attracted.

parameters.name: vacancy_phrase

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No vacancy matches that description, listed or removed.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the vacancies that match with the dates their postings ran.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one post. A removed posting can be named too — the record of what was advertised stays (BR-9, AC-9).

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period asked about.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Every listing and removal, and what each brought in.

fields.name: listings
fields.description: When it was listed, by whom, when it came off, why, and how many days it ran (BR-6).

fields.name: advertised_text
fields.description: The role and requirements the posting carried in each listing, as the vacancy held them at the time. This is the answer to a candidate asking afterwards what the post said (BR-3, BR-9).

fields.name: applications_per_listing
fields.description: How many applications each listing attracted (BR-4).

fields.name: removed_by_system
fields.description: Removals nobody chose — the closing date passing, or the vacancy being closed in recruitment while the posting was still up (BR-5, BR-11).

fields.name: relistings
fields.description: How many times the same post went back up. A post advertised three times is a post the school has not been able to fill.

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the posting history.
errors.note: The history screen is open to the School Admin, the Principal and the Super Admin.

planningRules.rule: Give what the posting said, not only when it ran. A candidate may ask afterwards what the post said, and that is the reason the record is kept at all (BR-3, BR-9, AC-9).

Separate removals nobody chose from removals somebody decided. A posting taken off by the closing date and one pulled because the post was filled read the same in a list and mean different things (BR-5, BR-11).
Name a post that was listed more than once. Three listings is a post the school has not been able to fill, and it is visible only across the history — never in what is on the site today.
Give applications against days listed. A listing that ran four days and one that ran a month are not compared by their totals (BR-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads cannot be edited by anybody, which is what makes it answerable to a candidate.

request.text: physics teacher ki posting kab lagi thi, kab hati aur kyun?
request.gloss: when was the physics teacher posting put up, when did it come down and why?

steps.note: One read, including the listing already removed (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the dates it ran, who listed it, who took it down and the reason — and what the posting said while it stood, since that is what a candidate would be asking about. Add the applications it attracted against the days it ran.

request.text: pichle saal kitni vacancies advertise hui thin aur kitni applications aayin?
request.gloss: how many vacancies were advertised last year and how many applications came in?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the listings with days run and applications each. Point out the posts listed more than once — a post advertised three times is one the school has not been able to fill, and that is visible nowhere else — and separate the postings the closing date took down from the ones somebody pulled because the post was filled.
